title: Check: Introduction to Rates of Reaction

questions.stem: In a reaction, 60 cm³ of gas is produced in 30 seconds. What is the average rate of reaction?
questions.explanation: Rate of reaction = amount of product formed ÷ time taken = 60 cm³ ÷ 30 s = 2 cm³/s. The rate tells us how much gas is produced per second.

questions.stem: On a graph of volume of gas produced against time, what does the gradient (slope) of the line represent?

options.text: The total amount of product formed
The rate of reaction at that point

questions.explanation: The gradient (slope) of a volume-time graph represents the rate of reaction at that point. A steeper gradient means a faster rate. The gradient is steepest at the start and decreases as reactants are used up, eventually reaching zero when the reaction is complete.
